taxonomyNote: Formerly Leptotyphlops humilis; NatureServe notes Adalsteinsson et al. (2009) moved North American threadsnakes to Rena.
fieldMarks: Very small, thin, earthworm-like snake; light purple, pink or brown.
Tail ends in a small spine; eyes are non-functional (often called a blind snake).
behavior: Secretive and fossorial; found under rocks, wood or debris, among roots or in crevices, often in loose damp soil.
Appears on the surface at night, especially after warm-season rains.
Eats ants and termites (following ant pheromone trails to nests), other small insects and their larvae and eggs, spiders, centipedes and millipedes.
Lays 2-6 eggs in July-August; females may stay with eggs and may nest communally.
habitat: Deserts and desert grasslands to brush-covered slopes: sand dunes, washes, rocky hillsides, canyon bottoms, riparian zones and areas near springs, sometimes gardens.
range: Southern California, southern Nevada and southwestern Utah south through Arizona, southern New Mexico and western Texas to southern Baja California and Colima, Mexico; from below sea level to about 1,520 m.
